title: How do you generate and use Allure/HTML test reports (passed/failed, duration, error messages, screenshots, videos, trace files, environment info), and why should a report help developers DIAGNOSE a failure rather than just show red/green?
shortTitle: Generating and using Allure/HTML reports that help developers diagnose failures
keyPoints: The built-in HTML reporter produces a self-contained site with on-failure screenshots, videos, and traces automatically embedded
Allure adds organizational features: suites, severity labels, history, trends, and the ability to attach arbitrary files
A diagnostic report carries status, duration, error messages, screenshots, video, traces, and environment info for each test
The Playwright trace is the most powerful artifact: DOM snapshots, network requests, and console logs at each step
Reports must enable diagnosis, not just scoring: a developer should identify the cause from the report without re-running
Always include environment and build metadata so failures can be classified as regressions vs environmental differences

s1_definition.oneliner: Generate Allure or HTML reports with status, duration, error details, screenshots, videos, traces, and environment info, and treat the report as a diagnosis tool so a developer can see why a test failed and fix it, not just that it is red.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **HTML reporter** – Built-in Playwright reporter producing a self-contained site with on-failure screenshots, videos, and traces.
- **Allure reporter** – Rich organizational features: suites, severity, history, trends, and arbitrary file attachments.
- **Diagnostic artifacts** – Screenshots at failure, video of the sequence, trace with DOM/network/console, error message and stack.
- **Environment info** – Browser, version, base URL, build commit. Lets developers classify regressions vs environmental differences.
- **Purpose** – Diagnosis, not scoring. A developer should identify the cause from the report without re-running the test.
s1_definition.analogy: When the National Bank of India's overnight tests run, a bare result that just says "something failed" is almost useless. A good report is like a detailed incident file: which step broke, a screenshot at that moment, a video of the whole attempt, a step-by-step trace, the exact error, and which environment and build it ran against.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Test Report as a Diagnosis Tool
  ────────────────────────────────

  Test Run
    │
    ├── PASSED tests: status + duration
    │
    └── FAILED tests: status + duration +
         │
         ├── Error message + stack trace
         ├── Screenshot (visual state at failure)
         ├── Video (full sequence)
         ├── Trace (DOM + network + console)
         ├── Named steps (which phase failed)
         └── Environment info (browser, URL, commit)
              │
              ▼
         Developer opens report
         -> Identifies cause in minutes
         -> No re-run needed
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
I generate reports with both the HTML reporter and Allure. The HTML reporter produces a self-contained site after each run, automatically embedding on-failure screenshots, videos, and traces. Allure adds suites, severity, history, trends, and arbitrary attachments for larger programs.

What makes a report useful is diagnosis, not just red/green. Every failure carries the error message and stack, a screenshot at the failure point, a video of the sequence, the Playwright trace with DOM, network, and console at each step, named steps so the report reads as a narrative, and environment metadata so failures can be classified as regressions vs environmental differences.

The reason reports must enable diagnosis is economics. A bare red/green forces re-running locally, which is slow and often impossible for CI-specific failures. A diagnostic report collapses that loop: a developer opens the report, views the trace, and identifies the cause in minutes without re-running.

At the National Bank of India an on-call engineer opened a failed transfer test's trace and immediately saw the balance API had returned an error, fixed it without ever reproducing locally.

Remember one sentence: a test report should carry enough evidence for someone who was not watching the run to diagnose the failure in minutes, not just show red or green.
